record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: What explains and resolves the remaining discrepancy between experiment and theory for neutrino interactions on carbon, especially for neutrinos produced from the decay-in-flight of pions, despite several years of theoretical and experimental effort?

evidence.quote: The most studied case, namely neutrino interactions on carbon, still suffer from a discrepancy between experiment and theory, in particular for the neutrinos produced from the decay-in-flight of pions, in spite of the efforts done during several years [18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current neutrino scattering on a $^{12}$C target. For muon-neutrinos produced via the decay-in-flight of positive pions ($\pi^+ 	o \mu^+ 
u_\mu$), with the corresponding energy spectrum, define the flux-averaged inclusive cross section
$$\langle \sigma angle_{m DIF} \;=\; \int dE_
u \, \phi_{m DIF}(E_
u)\, \sigma\!\left(
u_\mu + {}^{12}{m C} 	o \mu^- + Xight),$$
where $\phi_{m DIF}$ is the normalized $
u_\mu$ flux from $\pi^+$ decay-in-flight. Standard many-body nuclear calculations (continuum random phase approximation and related approaches) predict a value of $\langle \sigma angle_{m DIF}$ that exceeds the experimentally measured inclusive cross section by roughly $20$–$30\%$, in contrast to the corresponding inclusive $
u_e + {}^{12}{m C} 	o e^- + X$ cross section for $
u_e$ from $\mu^+$ decay-at-rest and to the exclusive $^{12}{m C}(
u_\mu,\mu^-){}^{12}{m N}_{m g.s.}$ transition, both of which agree with theory.

Identify and quantitatively account for the nuclear-physics mechanism (e.g., short- and long-range correlations, quenching of spin-isospin response, multinucleon and meson-exchange currents, final-state interactions, or shell-model configuration mixing) responsible for the residual discrepancy between theory and experiment in $\langle \sigma angle_{m DIF}$, and produce a consistent theoretical framework that simultaneously reproduces the measured inclusive and exclusive decay-in-flight and decay-at-rest cross sections on $^{12}$C.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent large-scale shell-model calculations of the inclusive $^{12}$C$(\nu_\mu,\mu^-)$ decay-in-flight cross section yield values reduced relative to CRPA, owing to quenching of the $1^+$ spin response and the restricted configuration basis, bringing predictions closer to LSND/KARMEN measurements. The exclusive channel is well reproduced, but a fully consistent theoretical description of all $\nu$-$^{12}$C inclusive data (especially decay-in-flight) remains under active investigation, with ongoing work on multinucleon currents and correlations. Hence the issue is partially, but not definitively, resolved.

status_evidence.title: Limits on electron neutrino disappearance from the KARMEN and LSND $\nu_e$-Carbon Cross Section Data
status_evidence.snippet: Cross section data on 12C from KARMEN and LSND used to constrain $\nu_e$ disappearance; ongoing reanalysis of carbon cross sections.
status_evidence.claim: The carbon cross section data remain a benchmark and subject of continued analysis, with residual tension affecting interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino-12C reactions and the LSND and KARMEN experiments on neutrino oscillations
status_evidence.snippet: Shell-model predictions reduce the decay-in-flight inclusive cross section relative to CRPA, improving agreement with experiment, while exclusive channels agree well.
status_evidence.claim: Large-scale shell-model calculations partially resolve the DIF discrepancy via quenching of spin modes.

status_evidence.title: PDG Review of Neutrino Cross Sections
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of low-energy neutrino-nucleus cross sections including 12C, noting remaining theoretical uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: A complete, universally accepted theoretical description of all inclusive $\nu$-$^{12}$C data is still lacking.
